xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-4311: CPU contention: weight the dashboard, nice batch agents, surface runaway processes, hold machine dispatch on CPU pressure

plan.title: CPU contention: weight the dashboard, nice batch agents, surface runaway processes, hold machine dispatch on CPU pressure
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

metadata.sizeJustification: One issue with one acceptance set: the three steps (weights+nice, runaway detector, CPU dispatch hold) share the resources.* config keys (cfg-keys), the PSI reader and stateless CPU check (cpu-psi-reader), and the governor's cpu trigger. The DAG has no edges between the three steps except through those shared foundations, so the work agent can fan them out in parallel. Splitting into sibling tracker issues is an operator action and was not taken in auto mode.

narratives.Problem: Load reached ~79 on the 24-core host (2026-09-28). A lane ran 42 `yes` processes; conversation 2884's `git log -S | head` outlived its timed-out Bash call and burned ~90% of a core for 95 minutes. The dashboard slowed and conversations loaded slowly. Overdeck has no working CPU protection: the governor's CPU hold gates nothing, no dispatch door reads CPU, app.slice has no cpu controller (dashboard competes per thread with every agent), every agent runs at nice 0, and the existing runaway attribution code (buildHostProcesses, spike sampler, history sampler) has no production input.
narratives.Proposal: (1) Weights and nice: CPUWeight=1000 on the dashboard transient unit and supervisor (enables the cpu controller in app.slice), CPUWeight=20 on verification scopes, and a nice prefix at launchAgentPane by CPU class (batch 10, lane 15, interactive conversations unchanged). (2) An observe-only runaway sampler started from the dashboard main process (30 s, async /proc reads) with a pure classifier (orphaned / detached-from-tool-shell / outlived-tool-call / long-burn at >=0.5 sustained cores over 10 min), transition-only warn/escalate/resolve feed entries, and real input for /api/resources hostProcesses and the spike sampler. (3) CPU PSI (/proc/pressure/cpu some avg60, load fallback): a cpu trigger in the governor feed, a stateless assessCpuPressure used by the lane door (429 unless --force), an acknowledgeable cpu_saturated guardrail warning, an opt-in Flywheel spawn hold (default off), PSI in quality-gate admission, and PSI in the (now wired) resource history plus a 5-minute calibration log line. Full detail, corrected references and snippets: PRD .pan/drafts/pan-4311.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Per-agent systemd scopes / overdeck-{conversations,agents,lanes}.slice and CPUWeight on the Herdr unit (renderHerdrUnit stays unchanged)
- Killing, pausing, stopping or messaging any process or agent automatically
- Gating conversations, operator pan start, or dashboard Start on CPU
- Enabling the Flywheel spawn hold by default (governor_cpu_hold_dispatch stays false)
- ionice, IOWeight, or CPUQuota anywhere
- Dashboard cpu.pressure in /api/metrics, nicing the dashboard's own children, CPU admission for other projects' tests, Docker cpu_shares
- Frontend UI changes
- New HTTP routes
- Running pan reload / pan up / pan restart from the workspace (the live cgroup check is a post-merge operator checkpoint)

autoDecisions.summary: Start the runaway sampler from dashboard main.ts next to startResourcesSnapshotService, not from the hygiene scheduler
autoDecisions.rationale: The hygiene scheduler runs in the deacon child process (deacon-main.ts:143 -> cloister/service.ts:348), so its module cache is invisible to /api/resources in main; the runtime mirror behind isIdle is also populated only in main.

autoDecisions.summary: Dispatch gates use a stateless assessCpuPressure() instead of the governor's cached verdict
autoDecisions.rationale: getCachedMemoryVerdict() is null outside the deacon child; the lane door and guardrail run in main and spawnAgent runs in the pan start CLI. A stateless PSI threshold check gives the same answer in every process; the governor's hysteresis stays for the feed only.

autoDecisions.summary: Flywheel spawn hold ships behind resources.governor_cpu_hold_dispatch, default false
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue body names this default; the 2026-08-02 swap-residency correction in memory-governor.ts records that holds on persistently elevated signals wedged the pipeline for weeks.

autoDecisions.summary: Exclude quality gates by derivable facts (verification scopes are not enumerated; leader nice 19 and age < 20.5 min) instead of the in-memory gate registry
autoDecisions.rationale: activeGateProcessGroups lives in the process that ran the gate and cannot be read cross-process; gates are always nice -n 19 and are group-killed by their watchdog after 20.5 min.

autoDecisions.summary: Resolve the harness pid from /proc comm/environ data rather than findAgentRuntimePidInSubtree
autoDecisions.rationale: The probe execs ps/pgrep per tree node, which would spawn hundreds of processes per 30 s tick; the sampler already reads comm, ppid and environ for every pid.

autoDecisions.summary: Wire recordResourceHistorySample from refreshResourcesSnapshot and add a 5-minute calibration line to deacon.log
autoDecisions.rationale: The history sampler has no production caller and keeps only 24 h in memory, so it cannot hold the week of PSI samples the issue wants for calibration; deacon.log is durable.

autoDecisions.summary: Derive the lane CPU class from the conversation row's laneRole inside spawnConversationSession
autoDecisions.rationale: Passing it only through the launch context would lose it on resume; laneRole is a write-once fact on the row.

autoDecisions.summary: evaluateSpawnGuardrails takes the CPU verdict as a second parameter (default null); spawn-gate.ts passes null
autoDecisions.rationale: Keeps the guardrail pure over its inputs; SystemHealthSnapshot carries no PSI.

autoDecisions.summary: The live cgroup/nice check (issue AC-0) is a post-merge operator checkpoint, not an xBRIEF acceptance criterion
autoDecisions.rationale: It needs a deploy via pan reload, which only the Flywheel/operator performs; work and test roles cannot observe it before merge.

autoDecisions.summary: Keep one issue and one plan with sizeJustification instead of filing sibling issues
autoDecisions.rationale: The operator filed one issue with one acceptance set; the steps share config keys, the PSI reader and the cpu trigger; creating tracker issues is an operator action. The DAG keeps the three steps parallel.

autoDecisions.summary: Quality-gate admission uses PSI some avg10 >= 25 (constant) with load/core >= 1 as fallback
autoDecisions.rationale: 25 matches the governor's recovery default: heavy test runs start only when the machine is back to the recovered level; avg10 matches the admission's short sampling horizon.

autoDecisions.summary: Conversations without runtime-mirror state never trigger the outlived-tool-call leg; the 30-minute long-burn backstop covers them
autoDecisions.rationale: liveness.isIdle returns false without runtime state; the backstop still catches the conv-2884 shape within 30 minutes.
